message.content:
The most recent estimate of the United States’ Gini coefficient—measuring income inequality on a scale from 0 (perfect equality) to 1 (perfect inequality)—is **about 0.41** (or 41 %).  

This figure comes from the OECD’s 2023 “Income Inequality” dataset, which uses the 2021 national income distribution data. The U.S. Gini has hovered around 0.40–0.42 for the past decade, reflecting a relatively high level of income inequality compared with many other OECD countries.
